A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same metric-convolution work. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison despite the revised title, expanded supplement and changed layout.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-denoising experiments, classification experiments on four datasets, and qualitative analyses, including supplementary results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds CIFAR-100 classification ablations and computational-resource measurements. Its imported FlexConv results are explicitly attributed to prior work.

M1.justification: The existing two-dimensional UTB/UGB procedures and Algorithms 1–3 are retained. Appendix B.2 adds a proposed higher-dimensional adaptation using d-dimensional metric tensors and spherical sampling coordinates, with grouped/depthwise variants. This extends the formulation without establishing changes to the original implemented algorithms.

E1.justification: Both versions use cameraman, BSDS300 and PascalVOC for denoising, and MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 for classification. The new experiments vary architectures and convolution configurations within this coverage; higher-dimensional applications are discussed but not evaluated.

E2.justification: v2 adds FlexConv/FlexNet-16 to the reported accuracy and timing comparisons in Tables 9–10, using results attributed to its original paper. The existing standard, dilated, shifted and deformable comparisons are retained. InternImage is discussed but is not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The original evaluation settings are retained. Appendix E.7 adds CIFAR-100 transfer-learning configurations with replacement restricted to layer4, ResNet18/50/152 architectures, and Randers versus Riemannian metrics. Table 9 adds peak-memory and per-epoch timing measurements. These are additional settings rather than documented revisions of the original experiments.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained denoising sensitivities, fixed/learned-weight comparisons and GradCAM analysis, Appendix E.7 adds systematic classification ablations of replacement depth, network depth and metric symmetry. Table 9 also examines computational overhead. These substantially expand the examination of central design choices and practical costs.

E5.justification: The original single-run MNIST/Fashion-MNIST results and eight-run CIFAR medians with standard deviations remain unchanged. New Table 11 reports means and standard deviations over ten independent runs per configuration. This is a new experiment's statistical protocol, not evidence that the original experiments received additional runs.

E6.justification: The original numerical tables and qualitative result panels are retained, but v2 adds substantial classification-ablation and resource results. Table 11 reports Randers top-1 accuracies of 74.20%, 79.17% and 80.56% for ResNet18/50/152 under the new setting. Table 9 reports 105 seconds and 1021 MB for metric convolutions versus 83 seconds and 940 MB for deformable convolutions. These are added results, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: v2 adds Theorem 3 and its shift-equivariance proof in Appendix D.5, including the periodic-padding assumption. Appendix B introduces higher-dimensional and multichannel formulations, parameterization arguments and conditions for extending beyond image domains. The earlier unification theorems, dual-metric derivation and differentiation formulas are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and three principal contribution statements remain essentially unchanged. The conclusion adds applicability to tasks requiring explicit pixel similarities, such as geodesic edge or tubular-structure extraction, and explicitly qualifies competitive performance by higher computational cost than standard convolution.

C2.justification: Appendix C.2 adds an extensive interpretation of modulation, weight sharing and differences from FlexConv. Appendix E.7 explains why replacement depth may depend on task scale and cautions against generalizing the small-task findings. v2 also adds interpretations of symmetry ablations, implementation costs and padding-dependent equivariance, substantially expanding applicability and mechanism discussion.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link and discloses peak GPU memory, per-epoch timings and deformable-CNN training time alongside the previously reported metric-CNN hardware and training duration. Most implementation algorithms, hyperparameters, preprocessing and training instructions are retained.

R1.justification: The existing research positioning is substantially expanded through the detailed FlexConv/modulation comparison in Appendix C.2 and the replacement-strategy discussion involving deformable-convolution variants and InternImage. Additional connections cover Finsler manifold learning, hyperbolic/Lorentz geometry and separable convolutions; these go beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The six-section main narrative and much of the original prose remain intact. v2 tightens wording, corrects terminology, updates the title and affiliations, adds acknowledgments and explanatory passages, and expands and renumbers appendix sections. Most of the expansion is new technical content rather than extensive rewriting of existing material.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column conference layout and separately numbered supplement. It adds geometric and procedural illustrations in Figures 1–2 and 7–13, a notation table, and Tables 9–11; Table 3 is reorganized. Existing result figures are retained but resized and relocated, producing a substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The shift-equivariance proof, architecture/metric ablations, clearer illustrations and code/resource disclosures make v2 easier to assess and use. The gains have limits: the FlexConv comparison imports results from a different model and does not establish matched protocols, while the new Appendix B.2 incorrectly counts a Cholesky factor's parameters as d(d−1)/2 rather than d(d+1)/2. Overall, the useful additions support a limited quality improvement.
